verdict.rationale: Plaid's Transactions docs say it retrieves up to 24 months of transaction data and stays current via webhooks, which covers history depth. The official Node SDK exposes a transactionsSync call, which points to a first-party sync endpoint. However, nothing in the pack describes pagination or cursor-based incremental 'only what changed' semantics. Missing for 10: documented pagination/cursor mechanics, explicit description of incremental change-only sync semantics (added/modified/removed), independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can pull transaction history for a connected account through the API — paginated, with documented history depth and a sync pattern for fetching only what changed

citations.quote: Retrieve up to 24 months of transaction data and stay up-to-date with webhooks
Plaid sends webhooks to programmatically inform you about changes to Plaid Items or the status of asynchronous processes.
